headline: Poland says Russian missiles hit its territory; Trump calls it a ‘mistake’
author: Mary Ilyushina

paragraphs.text: Russian missiles and a drone violated Polish airspace and crashed in the country’s southeast on Friday, according to Polish officials, who accused Moscow of a deliberate “provocation” and linked it to major military exercises by allied European countries preparing for a potential postwar mission in Ukraine.

“This doesn’t look like an accident,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. “We know for certain that what fell on Polish soil came from Russia.” Tusk said that foreign partners, including NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, shared that assessment.

President Donald Trump, however, shrugged off the alarm raised by Polish officials, saying that Russian President Vladimir “Putin has been landing drones in Poland and a couple of little missiles, by mistake.”
Officials said that one of the missiles was a Kh-101, a cruise missile that typically carries a warhead weighing 400 to 450 kilograms, or about 880 to 990 pounds.

The incident is the latest apparent violation of NATO airspace by Russian drones and missiles. The incursions have drawn outcry from European nations, but the alliance has so far largely followed Trump’s approach, playing down such incidents and refraining from retaliation against Moscow.

Drones have repeatedly strayed into European nations on NATO’s eastern flank during Russia’s war in Ukraine, fueling tension with the West and raising fears of a more direct conflict between Russia and the alliance. So far, no NATO ally has sought to invoke NATO’s collective defense clause over the incidents.
The military exercise was being held near Nowa Deba, about 60 miles from Poland’s border with Ukraine.

Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said in news conference Friday that two missiles and a jet-powered drone fell on Polish territory during Russia’s overnight airstrikes on Ukraine, all landing in the southeast.

One unspecified missile came down about 20 miles from where European troops were holding their military exercises, according to officials. The Kh-101 cruise missile crashed roughly 30 miles from the Ukrainian border, and what officials believe was a jet-powered drone hit the ground about 20 miles from the border.
No injuries or damage were reported.
The Kh-101 is among the most capable conventional weapons in Russia’s arsenal — a low-flying, generally hard-to-detect cruise missile launched from strategic bombers.

Moscow has used it extensively against Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, and it is built to hit its targets with precision, which means its landing on NATO territory raises more questions than the airspace violations by drones, which more frequently fly off-course.
The incident occurred a day after Putin, speaking at a news conference on Thursday following meetings with Trump and Xi Jinping in China, dismissed the idea that Russia poses a threat to Europe.

“The Americans keep urging us to mend our relations with Europe. But we never damaged those relations in the first place. Honestly, this political diarrhea needs to stop,” he said. “What is this talk about us attacking Europe? Everyone knows perfectly well that we have no desire for a war with Europe. What kind of nonsense is this?”

In China, Trump greeted Putin with a warm joke and called the Russian leader “my friend,” a remark that drew criticism from Western officials, including Poland’s Tusk, who posted on X: “God, protect us from such friends.”
The missiles came down in Poland amid a large-scale Russian air attack on Ukraine, which, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, killed at least eight people and left nearly 30 injured.

“The Russians spread this attack across many cities and regions of Ukraine. Absolutely all the targets were ordinary civilian infrastructure — things that literally sustain people’s lives,” Zelensky said.
The strikes on Ukraine came days after U.S.-brokered direct talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi last week — the first such discussions following a nine-month lull.

The two sides agreed only on humanitarian relief and appeared to remain far apart on other issues, as Russia also pressed to widen the discussion to the postwar security architecture in Europe, in line with the hard-line demands Russia sent the West in 2021. Back then, senior Russian officials denied any plans to invade Ukraine, but within weeks Putin ordered his troops across the border.

Europe has been under pressure to name delegates to participate in the talks, as Trump’s envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, push to bring European representatives into the next round of negotiations.
Russia has so far insisted there is no sense in engaging with Europe, which it describes as a “party to the war” because of its concerted military and financial support for Kyiv.

The Abu Dhabi talks were followed by a marked escalation. Ukrainian forces, in missile and drone strikes, destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge, collapsing part of it into the sea and rendering the structure unusable for road traffic.
Built by Russia after its invasion and illegal annexation of the Crimean Peninsula in 2014, the bridge is of huge symbolic importance to Putin, who has vowed to retaliate harshly.

“After the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, we will not negotiate,” Putin said at Thursday’s news conference in China. He claimed the bridge was used only for civilian purposes and that he had been considering agreeing to limited ceasefires in Ukraine until the Kerch road bridge was destroyed.
“We will respond to these attacks,” he said. “Our response will be far more painful than Kyiv’s attack on the bridge.”
On Friday, Russia launched a major attack across Ukraine, targeting bridges and railway stations in Kyiv overnight.

Zelensky has defended Ukraine’s repeated strikes on the Crimean Bridge, the main link between Russia and the occupied peninsula, calling them a “fair response” to what he says were 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges across Ukraine.
Zelensky told the BBC that the intense Russian attacks that followed the damage to the Crimean Bridge were a “signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate.”
